What about the Church?
Abraham Lincoln once said, ‘If all the people who fell asleep in 
church on Sunday morning were laid out end to end… they would 
be a great deal more comfortable.’ Before I became a Christian my 
heart used to sink when I heard the word ‘church’. The first thing 
that came to mind were church services: hard pews, unsingable 
tunes, enforced silences and excruciating boredom. A vicar was 
taking a small boy around his church one day and showing him the 
memorials. ‘These are the names of those who died in the Services.’ 
The boy asked, ‘Did they die at the morning service or at the 
evening service?’
Some associate the word ‘church’ with the clergy. Someone who is 
entering the ordained ministry is said to be ‘going into the church’.
